holidays.name: National Meatball Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate those round, saucy orbs of ground meat, whether they sit atop spaghetti, nestle in a sub sandwich, or get skewered on a toothpick at a party.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it grew out of food-industry and internet culture rather than any official proclamation. It is widely listed on March 9 by food-day calendars.
holidays.funFact: Meatballs show up in cuisines around the world, from Swedish köttbullar to Italian polpette to Middle Eastern kofta. Spaghetti and meatballs is largely an Italian-American invention.

holidays.name: Barbie Day
holidays.description: A pink-tastic celebration of the iconic fashion doll, her countless careers, and her Dreamhouse lifestyle.
holidays.origin: Barbie made her debut at the American International Toy Fair in New York City on March 9, 1959. Ruth Handler created her and named her after her daughter Barbara.
holidays.funFact: Barbie's full name is Barbara Millicent Roberts, and she has held more than 250 careers, including astronaut, surgeon, and presidential candidate.

holidays.name: Get Over It Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to letting go of grudges, old arguments, and that thing your cousin said at Thanksgiving three years ago. It is a reminder to move on and stop sweating the small stuff.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance, it has been listed on March 9 by quirky-holiday calendars as a prompt for emotional spring cleaning.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists say holding onto grudges can raise stress levels and blood pressure, so Get Over It Day may be good for your health too.

holidays.name: National Crabmeat Day
holidays.description: A day for seafood lovers to crack open some crab and enjoy sweet, buttery goodness in crab cakes, dips, bisques, or straight from the shell.
holidays.origin: It is a food-industry-style observance popularized by food holiday calendars, and it was likely created to promote crab consumption and seafood restaurants.
holidays.funFact: Crabs walk sideways because of the way their leg joints bend, and some species can move at surprising speeds when they need to.

holidays.name: National Napping Day
holidays.description: A day for those who survived the sleepy aftermath of Daylight Saving Time to take a guilt-free nap and recover lost sleep.
holidays.origin: It was created in 1999 by Boston University professor William Anthony and his wife Camille, who wanted to raise awareness about sleep deprivation. It falls on the Monday after clocks spring forward, so the date moves around each year and sometimes lands on March 9.
holidays.funFact: A power nap of 10 to 20 minutes can improve alertness and mood, and NASA studies found a 26-minute nap improved pilot performance by 34 percent.
